title: Necro-reaper: Pruning away Dead Memory Traffic in Warehouse-Scale Computers
problem: A significant fraction of memory traffic in warehouse-scale computers (WSC) is unnecessary: it consists of writebacks of deallocated (dead) heap data and fetches of uninitialized data, neither of which carries useful information. Short-lived heap allocations larger than a cache line—common in WSC—exacerbate this problem.
motivation: Memory bandwidth is a critical and growing bottleneck in warehouse-scale computing, and eliminating provably dead traffic can improve throughput and IPC without changing application semantics.
method: Necro-reaper combines software and hardware. A compiler uses profiling data (measurements from running real code) to analyze how long each chunk of memory stays allocated, then inserts special CPU instructions at allocation sites. A customized memory allocator uses these instructions to signal the hardware when memory is deallocated. The hardware then skips unnecessary memory traffic for dead regions without needing its own logic to track which data is still in use.
key_novelty: Special CPU instructions allow the compiler and memory allocator to signal dead heap memory to the hardware, which then skips unnecessary writebacks and fetches without needing its own tracking.
contributions: Identification and quantification of dead memory traffic (needless writebacks and uninitialized-data fetches) as a major WSC bottleneck
New ISA instructions enabling software-directed avoidance of dead memory traffic
Profile-guided compiler pass that annotates heap allocation/deallocation sites with dead-traffic-avoidance instructions
WSC-scale evaluation across 10 workloads showing 26% geomean memory traffic reduction and 6% geomean IPC gain

metrics.speedup: 6% geomean IPC increase across 10 WSC workloads

baselines: baseline without dead-traffic elimination (prior work requiring hardware tracking)
limitations: The approach requires WSC-style vertical integration (co-designed hardware, compiler, and allocator); applicability to commodity off-the-shelf systems is limited.
primary_theme: software-hardware co-design to eliminate dead memory traffic in warehouse-scale computers
